title: Central Carolina Presbytery (Memorial) Louisiana Presbytery
disposition_detail: Sustained the Central Carolina Memorial: Part I Issues 1 and 2 answered Yes, and Issue 3 found Louisiana Presbytery had not demonstrated due diligence and had not met its responsibilities under BCO 13-9.f and 40-4/40-5; amends directed Presbytery to examine TE Wilkins, keep full records, adopt formal responses with rationale, note inconsistencies, and report by February 16, 2007. Overruled Louisiana Presbytery's objections to the proceedings. Part II Issue 1 answered Yes on procedural compliance; Issue 2 answered No expressly by reference to Case 2007-8 Judgment 2, which found probable error. Amends cited Louisiana Presbytery under BCO 40-5 to show what it had done or failed to do, appointed RE Samuel J. Duncan as prosecutor, and designated Case 2007-14 for indictment and possible trial. No original jurisdiction under BCO 34-1 was assumed.
first_summary: Central Carolina Presbytery memorialized the SJC, alleging Louisiana Presbytery wrongly exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite published teachings against the Westminster Standards. The SJC found the allegations grave and Presbytery lacking due diligence, ordered further examination and report, then later found procedural compliance but cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5 for substantive failure, appointing a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.
summary: In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.

evidence_notes.dispute: Central Carolina’s BCO 40-5 memorial, lines 21–94, alleged Louisiana Presbytery exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite published views on election, visible/invisible church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism contrary to the Westminster Standards, and failed to condemn erroneous opinions under BCO 13-9.f. SJC stated the issues at lines 110–116 and 311–315.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Part I: Issues 1–2 Yes; Issue 3 found no demonstrated due diligence and failure under BCO 13-9.f/40-4/40-5, with amends at lines 118–172. Reasons included no committee minutes or transcript, no face-to-face examination, a report addressing Federal Vision generally, no rationale for exoneration, and no mandated correction (lines 128–150). Part II: Issue 1 Yes on procedural compliance; Issue 2 No by reference to 2007-8 Judgment 2; BCO 40-5 citation and Case 2007-14 amends at lines 319–335.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC stressed it was reviewing Presbytery’s handling, not trying TE Wilkins personally, and did not proceed under BCO 34-1 (lines 313–323, 331–335). Procedural compliance did not establish substantive conformity. Vote count: 20 qualified, 2 absent, 2 recused, 0 disqualified (line 341); Part I vote 17 concurring and 7 absent (line 176).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Case 2007-8 is incorporated by reference: its Judgment 2 found probable error/violation of BCO 13-9.f, 40-4, and 40-5 for failure to find a strong presumption of guilt (lines 321–323, 331). The source does not include the full 2007-8 record but supplies that result. Case 2007-14 was designated for the new BCO 40-5 citation (line 323).
